best_plan.name: p1
best_plan.rationale: p1 is the best plan because it was the only executed plan to achieve perfect retrieval quality (f1_score 1.0). Although p3 was somewhat cheaper and faster, it dropped to 0.8 quality, and the lower-cost nano plans also lost accuracy. Since the task asks for five correct positive reviewIds, p1 offers the safest cost-quality trade-off.

cost_model_explanation: The cost model helped compare several semantic-filter variants before execution and showed that the exact Python filter on idx was essentially free while the sem_filter dominated both cost and latency. Restricting the LLM to depends_on=["reviewText"] kept the semantic call narrower. Cheaper models like Gemini Flash Lite and GPT-5 Nano reduced dollar cost, but observed runs showed they also reduced quality, so the slightly more expensive GPT-4.1 Nano plan was worth it here.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: str(row["idx"]).strip().lower() == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_filter(
    "This review is overall positive toward the movie.",
    model=pz.Model.GPT_4_1_NANO,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.project(["reviewId"])
pipeline.limit(5)
pipeline
